modern: He who runs away from his master is a runaway; but the law is master, and he who breaks the law is a runaway. And he too who is grieved or angry or afraid is dissatisfied because something has been or is or will be of the things which are appointed by him who rules all things, and he is Law, and assigns to every man what is fitting. He, then, who fears or is grieved or is angry is a runaway.
original: He who flies from his master is a runaway; but the law is master, and he who breaks the law is a runaway. And he also who is grieved or angry or afraid, is dissatisfied because something has been or is or shall be of the things which are appointed by him who rules all things, and he is Law and assigns to every man what is fit. He then who fears or is grieved or is angry is a runaway.

explained.summary: A slave who flees his master is a runaway, and the law of the universe is a master too, so whoever breaks it is a runaway. Marcus goes further. When you grieve, rage or fear, you’re objecting to something past, present or future that has been assigned by whatever rules all things, which is law itself, giving each person their due. So giving way to fear, grief or anger is a kind of desertion.
